title: Minimum Positive Sum Subarray
statement: Consider every contiguous, non-empty block of `nums` whose length is at least `l` and at most `r`. Among those blocks whose total is strictly positive, find the smallest total and return it. If no block in that length range adds up to more than 0, return `-1`.
signature: int minimumSumSubarray(List<Integer> nums, int l, int r)
notes:
## Intuition

With at most 100 numbers there are only about 5,000 blocks, so checking all of them is fast. The only work per block is its total, and a prefix-sum array turns that into one subtraction: the total of `nums[start..start+size-1]` is `prefix[start + size] - prefix[start]`.

## Approach

1. Build `prefix`, where `prefix[i]` is the sum of the first `i` numbers.
2. For every `start`, try every `size` from `l` to `r` that still fits in the array.
3. Read the block's `sum` from the prefix array. If it is positive and below `best`, keep it.
4. Return `best`, or `-1` if it was never set.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3, -2, 1, 4]`, `l = 2`, `r = 3`, so `prefix = [0, 3, 1, 2, 6]`.

- `start = 0`: size 2 gives `1 - 0 = 1` (new `best`), size 3 gives `2`.
- `start = 1`: size 2 gives `-1` (not positive), size 3 gives `3`.
- `start = 2`: size 2 gives `5`; size 3 runs past the end.
- `start = 3`: even size 2 runs past the end.

The smallest positive total is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · (r - l + 1)): one subtraction per pair of start and size.
- Space: O(n) for the prefix array.

## Pitfalls

- A total of exactly 0 does not count; the test is `sum > 0`.
- Stop growing `size` once `start + size` passes `n`, or the subtraction reads past the array.
- Start `best` at `Infinity` and turn it into `-1` only at the end: starting at `-1` would make `sum < best` always false.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `prefix` | `prefix[i]` is the sum of `nums[0..i-1]` |
| `start` | first index of the block |
| `size` | length of the block, from `l` to `r` |
| `sum` | total of the current block |
| `best` | smallest positive total found so far |

narration.3: prefix[0] is the sum of no numbers at all.
narration.4: Walk through the numbers once to build the running totals.
narration.5: Each new prefix sum is the previous one plus the next number.
narration.7: Infinity means no positive block has been found yet.
narration.8: Enumerate every index where a block can start.
narration.9: Try each allowed length from l to r, stopping once the block would run past the end.
narration.10: The block's total is the difference of two prefix sums.
narration.11: Only a strictly positive total counts, and it must beat the best so far.
narration.12: Remember the new smallest positive total.
narration.16: Report -1 if no block qualified, otherwise the smallest positive total.
